1 Shoulder join and lats

The double-biceps shoulder, rebuilt. Same pose, same light, before and after, then the round-three lat trim for her.

Before · v1 (arm separates from the body)

After · male

After · female

What was wrong

In the double-biceps pose the upper arm turns 86°, and the deltoid was part of the arm, so it turned with it and ended up as a lens along the top of the arm. That left nothing over the joint: the round end of the arm lay on the pec corner as a visible edge, and a gap opened between the trapezius and the arm.

What changed

  • Shoulder cap. A new deltoid dome lives on the torso side of the joint and is drawn over the arm root, so the arm tucks under it. Its top edge continues the trapezius line into the top of the arm.
  • Lat wing. A lat wing fills the armpit and widens the V under the raised arm, so the torso flows out into the arm instead of stopping at the ribs. It was reworked in rounds two and three (see below).
  • Rig. Both are separate groups pivoted at the shoulder (cap, flare), so the cap can turn at half the arm's angle when you animate relaxed to flex. They are also used by the lateral raise below.

  • Male. Unchanged from v3.
  • Rig. Still a separate flare group per side, pivoted at the shoulder.

How she differs from him

  • Silhouette. Shoulders are 15% narrower, the waist drops to 56% of shoulder width (male 62%) and the hips flare, so she is athletic, not a re-skinned male.
  • Muscle. Every plane is shrunk about 10% and the arms and calves are about 15% slimmer. The abs, serratus and quads are still defined so she can carry every activation view below. Rounds 3 and 4 trimmed her lat wing, shortened her shorts and softened her glutes; round 5 widened her hips.
  • Wardrobe. I treated "no shirt" as a male rule and gave her a top. It is one charcoal group (bra, bust, strap), so it is trivial to remove or recolour. Round 4 slimmed the straps and trimmed the top; the padded push-up is compared with it in section 7. The bralette was dropped.
  • Ponytail. A separate pony segment pivoted on the head, so it can swing in animation. In the front view it falls over the viewer's right shoulder.

4 Activations

The same Cobalt Sculpt muscle planes, recoloured by role. No new shapes are needed for the front and side views: an activation is just a fill on the existing muscle, so a film can keyframe it per beat. Muscles that sit under the shorts (glutes, hip flexors) appear as translucent overlays. The muscles of the back are lit in the back views in section 8.

How to read it Prime mover: coral plane with a soft halo Secondary / assisting: marigold Stabiliser: pale cobalt Idle: the normal cobalt plane Numbered badges mark the prime movers and match the list under each figure (toggle them in the bar).

5 Running activations ankle slider

A four-pose gait on the same rig (generic forward kinematics, so each pose is just a set of joint angles). The near leg is shown with the full activation; the far side is dimmed as usual but still lit when it is the driver. The flame stays upright in the air. New in round 5: you can change the ankle angle of every running figure below.

Ankle angle Minus lifts the toes (dorsiflexion), plus points them (plantar flexion). It is added to each phase's own foot angle, and the shoe turns about the ankle joint.

6 Faces

Faceless is the default for the whole character. Minimal and Ember visor are kept as secondary options (Soft features is dropped). Each face is one small group inside the head segment (translate(0,-92) in head coordinates), so it can be swapped or removed without touching the body.

·

Faceless default

Default · used on every figure in this document

The approved Cobalt Sculpt head: a smooth hood with a slightly lighter face plane and no features. The ponytail, the spark and the body language carry the character.

Good for animation

  • Nothing to animate wrong: the pose does all the acting
  • Reads at any size and keeps him and her equally neutral
  • Lets the narrator, not the character, carry emotion

Costs

  • No eye line, so a character looking at something needs a posture cue
  • No mouth, so narration cannot be lip-synced
A

Minimal secondary

Secondary option

Two oval eyes with a catch-light and a small smile on the existing face plane. Nothing else changes.

Good for animation

  • Cheapest rig: two eyes and one mouth, and the head stays the approved hood
  • Reads at 64 px and stays closest to the faceless character
  • Her lash flick is the only gender cue on the face

Costs

  • Little range: effort and fatigue need brows added
  • Smooth hood plus dots can feel toy-like
C

Ember visor secondary

Secondary option

A dark visor plane with marigold glowing eyes and a tiny smile, echoing the spark.

Good for animation

  • Strongest brand tie (marigold on cobalt) and the best contrast, so it reads at the smallest size
  • Eyes can pulse, squint or glow brighter for effort
  • Lowest chance of an off-model face

Costs

  • Closest to the old mask-face, so it risks reading as a robot again
  • A mouth is only a hint, so it needs a lip-sync set later

How they are built

  • Each bra is a variant of her chest segment (chest_sport and chest_push) with the same muscle planes underneath. The bra, the lighter cup planes and the straps are separate charcoal shapes, so a bra can be swapped or recoloured without touching the body.
  • Both end on the same marigold hem line as before, so the abs, the lower ribs and the waist read the same whichever you choose.
  • Sports top: the simplest shape and the most robust at small sizes. Push-up: the clearest feminine silhouette, with padding that projects in profile, but it covers more of the chest.
  • In the activation poses the chest planes are only partly visible under either bra, which is the same trade-off the sports top had.

How the back is built

  • Same skeleton. The back view reuses the front silhouettes, pivots and joint topology, so any pose, activation or animation that works from the front works from behind. Only the interior (muscle planes, lines, cloth) is new, in rig_back.
  • New muscle planes. Trapezius (kite), infraspinatus and teres, lats, erector spinae, hamstrings (two heads), gastrocnemius (two heads) and a Y of back straps; the shoulder cap is the rear deltoid and the raised arm shows the triceps horseshoe.
  • Shorts from behind. A centre seam and two raised seat planes, with the glute activation drawn as a translucent overlay on them, as in the side view.
  • Her hair. The ponytail hangs in front of the head from behind and swings to the viewer's right, so the spine and left trapezius stay readable.
  • Trainers. A heel view with a pull tab and a stitch line. No logo.

Back activations

  • The three cards use the same role colours as sections 4 and 5. Rear double biceps lights the lats and trapezius; the reverse fly lights the rear deltoid and infraspinatus; the deadlift lockout lights the posterior chain.
  • The rhomboids sit under the trapezius, so they are not drawn on their own; the trapezius plane stands in for them.
  • Back views exist for the relaxed, double-biceps and arms-out poses. A running or squatting pose from behind would reuse the same data and is a small step.

9 Still imperfect

Things I know are not done, so you can weigh them before choosing a direction.

Drawing

  • Hands: the front hand now has four separate fingers and a thumb, but there are no finger joints. The fist and the side-view hand are still simple shapes.
  • The far limbs in side and running poses are mirrored copies, dimmed on purpose to read as farther away. They are not separate drawings.
  • Bra straps are straight, rigid strips on every figure. The racerback straps are straight too.
  • The ankle slider turns the whole shoe as one piece. Past about 35° the foot looks rigid because the sole does not bend at the toes and the heel does not rise.
  • Back views: no running or squatting pose yet, no face (there is none to see), and the rhomboids are not drawn separately.

Choices to confirm

  • Back-view poses: are relaxed, double biceps and arms-out enough, or do you want back running and squat poses too?
  • Faces: faceless is the default. If you want Minimal or Ember visor, a mouth-shape set for narration comes next.
  • Seat highlight: the shorts show two raised seat planes from behind. If it reads as too much, removing the two seat shapes is a two-line change in the back data.
  • Activation colours: coral for prime, marigold for secondary, pale cobalt for stabilisers. Easy to change.
